qc_j_fin_du_monde.blurb: Fin du monde is the last wall along the line of sectors at Chez Roger, a cliff in the Lanaudière region reached by a trail of roughly twenty minutes from the car park. It holds 19 routes, mostly bolted lines (13) with six traditional ones. The grades stay moderate to middling: a handful from 5.6 to 5.8, a few at 5.9, and about half the routes at 5.10. That makes it a good fit for climbers who lead around 5.9 and want a quieter wall at the far end of the crag, rather than a place to push the top of their range.

qc_lya.blurb: Lya is a small set of urban boulders inside Parc des Hirondelles in Montreal, tucked behind the basketball courts toward the middle of the park. You can drive to it, and two city bus lines also stop nearby. The 19 problems cover a very wide range, from V0 up to V9: a few friendly ones for kids and beginners, a solid middle band around V3 and V4, and a group of V6 and harder lines for strong boulderers. It suits a short session close to town, with a pad and ordinary outdoor bouldering gear.

qc_tranchant_middle.blurb: The central section of Montagne du Tranchant, near Saint-Côme in Lanaudière, with a shaded platform at the foot of the wall. It has 19 routes split between sport (12) and traditional (7), including a few of two or three pitches. Grades run from very easy up to the low 5.12s, with the greatest concentration at 5.10. Gentler lines sit on an angled block to the left, while the steeper headwall holds many of the best-rated climbs. A good all-round sector for mixed parties, as long as someone in the group is comfortable leading around 5.10.

qc_e_mur_principal_ad_nosine.blurb: The biggest and most imposing sector at Baldy, above Sainte-Adèle in the Laurentians. This is a steep, overhanging wall with a large ledge cutting across the left-hand routes. Nearly all of its 19 lines are bolted; one is traditional. The grades start around 5.11 and are concentrated in the 5.12s and 5.13s, with a few harder ones above that, so it is a place for strong, powerful sport climbers rather than for newcomers. The cliff as a whole gets shade from mid-afternoon in summer, which makes warm days more pleasant.

qc_secteur_principal.blurb: The main sector of Côtémis, a cliff in the Témiscamingue part of Abitibi-Témiscamingue a few kilometres south of Ville-Marie, and the obvious one to start with on arrival. It has 19 routes: about ten traditional and nine bolted. Grades span from 5.6 to 5.12, with a good number of easy and moderate lines, a cluster around 5.9 and 5.10, and a few harder ones at 5.11 and 5.12. Local climbers describe some of the trad lines as protected by sport-style bolts. A varied choice for a mixed group looking for a day in a remote part of the province.

qc_twin_ribs_down_under.blurb: Down Under is the right-hand rib of the Twin Ribs in Gatineau Park, close to Ottawa and Gatineau. It faces north and the wall is steep and overhanging, with bouldery moves on highly featured granite. All 19 routes are bolted. The grades sit mostly between 5.11 and 5.13, with one route at the very top of the range and a lone 5.10 for the warm-up, so it is a place for experienced sport climbers rather than beginners. It is regarded as the home of hard sport climbing in the Ottawa area.
